title: Trust-registry root-key rotation and compromise recovery
bounded_claim: On the tested same-host SQLite/OpenSSL prototype, root trust rotation R1->R2 and R2->R3 remained monotonic under the preregistered vectors.
A revoked historical root remained usable for historical cryptographic verification but was denied new currently eligible registry issuance after revocation.

Root epoch rollback, stale pre-rotation root snapshots, root identity/public-key substitution, old-root semantic rebinding, transition rebinding, and revoked-root plus registry-writer collusion failed closed in the tested vectors.
Exact transition replay remained idempotent and current-root restart preserved eligible replay and liveness.
No tested model, reviewer, registry writer, or revoked root acquired release or production authority.
observed_non_endpoint_hygiene: ResourceWarning messages for unclosed subprocess stdin/stdout handles were observed. They did not change any frozen endpoint and were preserved rather than repaired after first green exposure.
not_proven: Atomic crash recovery across the root-trust record store and the independent trusted-minimum store.
A physically simultaneous root-rotation commit racing current-root issuance at the exact transition boundary.
Physical host failure, disk power-loss semantics, or multi-host consensus.
Separate administrative or cloud trust domains.
Containment after compromise of both root-trust authentication material and trusted-minimum authority.
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 15: abrupt external process termination and recovery across root-trust rotation plus trusted-minimum advancement. Use parent-observed readiness and external termination around the two durable authorities, reopen in fresh processes, and test fail-closed ambiguity handling, exact replay, old-root non-resurrection, same-transition conflict prevention, and clean higher-root liveness.
